subject.title: feat: serve signed publisher feed projections

question: Should ClawHub approve a signed public-feed trust rollout that changes the existing catalog-feed representation and depends on production signing-secret/public-key provisioning, or require a backward-compatible transition first?
rationale: The patch changes a public API and signing trust boundary; deciding whether existing clients may be broken, and how production key provisioning is sequenced, requires maintainer ownership rather than an automated code repair.

options.title: Stage the contract and rollout
options.body: Keep this draft paused until the prerequisite feed and signing PRs are independently reviewed and merged, then rebase a narrow public-route layer with an approved compatibility plan.

options.title: Require a compatible transition
options.body: Retain the raw existing route and expose the DSSE response through a versioned route or explicit content negotiation, with proof for both representations.

options.title: Approve a coordinated breaking rollout
options.body: Accept the representation change only after maintainers confirm all consumers, production secret provisioning, public-key distribution, and rollback ownership.

recommendation.title: Stage the contract and rollout
recommendation.body: Keep this draft paused until the prerequisite feed and signing PRs are independently reviewed and merged, then rebase a narrow public-route layer with an approved compatibility plan.
